name: Ingrid Solberg
headline: 34, owner of a smoked-fish company, Bergen
title: The Empty Coffee Tin
situation: At 6:15 AM, Ingrid has just started the smokers and touched the iron bolt on the windowsill. Her morning ritual is simple: one strong cup of black coffee, drunk alone at the loft's east window while she watches the fjord. Today, the coffee tin is empty. The nearest open place is a small bakery two blocks away, but the owner is talkative and always tries to draw Ingrid into small talk. Ingrid prefers the quiet of the empty loft. She stands with the tin in her hand, deciding whether to spend the extra ten minutes walking through the cold, damp street for a proper cup, or to skip coffee and start her spreadsheet review early.

context.relationship_profiles:
The bakery owner, Marta, has known Ingrid since Ingrid was a child on the docks, and she still asks after Ingrid's father and the sold boat; their conversations always steer past coffee into family.
With Håkon and Mette, Ingrid has a standing agreement that pricing spreadsheets go out before the coast markets open, and they do not question her timing.
context.tendencies:
On mornings when the first smoker batch is running, she has usually postponed coffee and breakfast until after the initial temperature check.
When she needs to avoid interruptions, she has often turned off her phone and worked through the dawn hours rather than step outside.
She has a habit of rationing coffee beans and writing the order date on the tin, so an empty tin is rare.
context.current_state:
She slept no more than five hours after the last caregiver phone call about her father's insulin.
Her hands are still cold from touching the iron bolt and turning on the smokers, and her throat is dry.
She is carrying the day's schedule in her head: brine test at 7 AM, spreadsheet review, then a visit to her father before noon.
context.immediate_memories:
Looking at the empty tin, she remembers the morning three weeks ago when she found the same tin empty and decided to clean the smokehouse racks instead of getting coffee.
The east window view of the fjord brings back a calm morning when her father poured her a cup from his thermos on the boat, before the dementia worsened.
context.reflective_memories:
She recalls her grandmother's rule that a producer should never waste daylight on idle talk, a lesson repeated every season at the salting shed.
She also remembers that her father always shared coffee with the crew during breaks, treating the thermos as a way to hear what was happening on the docks.
